newsitem.title: GERMANY: J&J pays $14 mln to German group - magazine says.
newsitem.headline: J&J pays $14 mln to German group - magazine says.

text.p: A German magazine on Wednesday reported that U.S. drugs and consumer group Johnson & Johnson agreed to pay $14 million to German drugs group Boehringer Mannheim to settle a case of alleged inappropriate competitive activity.
In its latest edition, German magazine Wirtschaftswoche said the U.S. group had agreed to pay $14 million for an out-of-court settlement ending a five year battle.

Boehringer Mannheim spokesman Martin Kunzler confirmed an agreement had been reached in January between the privately held German group and the U.S. drugs group but declined to comment on the settlement.
"Both partners agreed not to speak about the amount, but I think the $14 million sum is likely," Kunzler said.

Boehringer Mannheim in January issued a statement saying only the two groups had "agreed to settle the issues that led last year to claims and counterclaims alleging inappropriate competitive activitiy."
Johnson & Johnson was not immediately available for comment.
